title: Private health-insurance enrollment concentration can narrow issuer choice while premium and care effects remain unmeasured
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-27-108927 review of private health-insurance market concentration from 2011 through 2024
geography: United States individual, small-group, large-group, and individual-exchange private health-insurance markets across states and the District of Columbia

observations.period: 2011–2024 enrollment series and October 16, 2026 GAO report

denominator.unit: states and the District of Columbia examined for issuer enrollment concentration

concentration_definition.value: GAO considers a state market concentrated when three or fewer issuers hold at least 80 percent of enrollment

2024_concentration.value: three or fewer issuers held at least 80 percent of enrollment for the individual and employer-group markets in at least 36 states

individual_market_trajectory.value: individual-market concentration generally increased from 2011 through 2024, peaked in 2019, and became slightly less concentrated afterward

exchange_trajectory.value: individual exchanges were concentrated in 47 states in 2015, peaked at 51 states in 2020, and were concentrated in 49 states in 2024
exchange_trajectory.unit: reported states and District of Columbia with three-or-fewer issuer concentration

market_scope.value: GAO examined individual, small-group, large-group, and individual-exchange markets using issuer enrollment data from 2011 through 2024

consumer_conversion.unit: issuer choice, premiums, plan quality, provider access, claims, medical care, employer wages, household burden, or health outcomes

observations.method: Structured extraction from GAO-27-108927, based on enrollment data issuers reported to CMS, state enrollment data collected by GAO for 2015–2017, and prior GAO analyses presented as a 2011–2024 series. Concentration definition, state-market share, individual and exchange trajectories, market scope, and consumer outcomes are retained as separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: Enrollment concentration is an indicator of issuer market structure, not a direct estimate of competition, premiums, network quality, provider access, or health outcomes. The state-level analysis does not establish effects for every enrollee, employer, plan, or local insurance market, and small changes in issuer counts do not by themselves show improved consumer welfare.
observations.subgroup: People buying individual coverage, workers and dependents in small- and large-group plans, employers, health-care providers, and households with different state-market and plan-choice conditions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Concentration can reflect scale economies, insurer entry and exit, risk-pool conditions, or plan differentiation; individual-exchange concentration eased after 2020, and a concentrated enrollment market may still contain meaningful plan, network, subsidy, or regulated-choice differences.

related_sources.claim: The official accessible report contains the market-concentration definition, 2011–2024 enrollment series, and individual-exchange comparison.
The official interactive graphic provides the state-level concentration comparison described by GAO.

boundary: This record advances a bounded private-health-insurance enrollment-concentration route. It does not establish issuer choice loss for individual consumers, premium effects, plan quality, provider access, claims, medical care, employer wages, household burden, or health outcomes.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Canonical GAO product URL string used as a stable source identifier; accessible report and interactive graphic links are retained for reproduction.
